solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Employer backs right side to rise once more

indicators.note: backs tells us to read the employer word from its end to its start

parts.note: someone who employs a thing is its user
a face is one side of a solid or a cliff

explanation.surface: An employer turns their back on the right-wing side of the business, hoping to rise again.
explanation.definitionFit: A diver or submarine coming up to the top of the water again does exactly this, rising once more.

clue.text: Maverick's trembling heart in dance

indicators.note: in places the heart of trembling inside the dance

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, here of the nine-letter trembling

explanation.surface: A maverick dancer with a nervous, trembling heart takes the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A maverick is an independent nonconformist who goes against the group, the same as a dissenter or insurgent.

clue.text: This courgette contains a pest

indicators.note: contains signals that the letters sit inside the run of words This courgette

explanation.surface: A gardener finds a grub lurking inside a courgette.
explanation.definitionFit: A persistent cause of trouble or affliction, like a plague, is called a pest or a curse.

clue.text: Rise up out of a single berth

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
out of says the letters are taken from inside the words single berth

explanation.surface: Someone rises up and climbs out of a single bunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise up' reads as one phrase, but 'up' is the reversal signal: the letters run backwards in singLE BERth.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise against authority is to revolt, so the verb sense of insurgency fits.

clue.text: Slowly, an Italian poet also bet a tanned complexion may be at an end

parts.note: Dante Alighieri wrote the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: An Italian poet wagers that his suntan will soon fade.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog finds four wordplays: AN + DANTE; AND + ANTE ('also bet'); 'complexion' rearranging TANNED; and 'may be' rearranging AT AN END.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the musical tempo marking for a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: European starts to leave union in a very short while — for a fee

indicators.note: in puts the initials of leave and union inside the short while

parts.note: a moment is a very brief space of time

indicators.note: starts to takes the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A European leaves the union in a flash, but only if paid for it.
explanation.definitionFit: An emolument is a salary, payment or fee received for work or holding an office.

clue.text: Chases sausages when hot

definitions.meaning: to follow someone persistently, as a hound would
hot frankfurters in rolls are hot ___, so this is the word that follows hot

explanation.surface: Chasing after sausages while they are still hot.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow doggedly is to pursue; and frankfurters in buns are hot dogs, so sausages are the second word.

clue.text: Place where film shows doctor starting to inject blood vessel

indicators.note: starting to takes the first letter of inject

parts.note: a vein carries blood back to the heart

explanation.surface: A doctor begins to inject a vein, as a film demonstrates.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive-in is an open-air cinema where people watch movies from their parked cars.

clue.text: Mira may be putting Goliath and his ilk on pitch

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so the giants come first

parts.note: Goliath was a biblical giant, so he and his kind are giants
pitch is a black sticky substance, the same as tar

explanation.surface: The setter, Goliath, imagines himself and fellow giants out on a sports pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Goliath is also the setter's pseudonym. 'Mira may be' signals a definition by example: Mira is a red giant in the constellation Cetus.
explanation.definitionFit: Mira is a red giant, a huge luminous stellar body, so it is one example of the type.

clue.text: Took in a graduate for an alternative place to sleep

parts.note: a BS is a Bachelor of Science graduate in American usage
or introduces an alternative
a bed is a place to sleep

explanation.surface: Someone takes in a graduate lodger, offering an alternative place to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak up or assimilate something, whether liquid or information, is to take it in.

clue.text: I'm surprised contents of Dior bag end in Buckeye

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: contents of takes the inner letters of each of the three words Dior, bag and end

explanation.surface: Exclaiming in surprise at what is inside a Dior handbag found in Buckeye country.
explanation.walkthrough: Buckeye looks like part of the surface's location, but it is the definition; 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckeye is the nickname for a native or resident of Ohio, the Buckeye State, named after its horse-chestnut tree.

clue.text: More than one almost tempt friend to come round

indicators.note: come round tells us the friend word surrounds the shortened tempt word

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: almost drops the last letter of the tempting word

parts.note: to lure is to tempt

explanation.surface: A friend is tempted, almost, to drop round for a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical number for nouns that denotes several items rather than a single one.

clue.text: Revolt in Gaza Netanyahu finally settled? Not quite

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of each of the words in, Gaza and Netanyahu
not quite removes the last letter of the settled word

parts.note: seated means settled in place

explanation.surface: A question about whether a revolt in Gaza was finally resolved for Netanyahu.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolt looks like a noun (an uprising) but is used as a verb meaning to sicken.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolt someone is to disgust them, making them feel sick.

clue.text: Have a preoccupation to back some bosses bothering other bosses

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read from right to left
some indicates only a portion of the words bosses bothering is used

explanation.surface: Some bosses fixate on pestering other bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run backwards across 'bosSES BOthering'; 'other bosses' only completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fixated on something, filling one's mind continually, is the verb meaning to have a preoccupation.

clue.text: Want first of several tequilas in pub, matter of theory

indicators.note: in places the want and the initials inside the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
to want is to lack

indicators.note: first of takes the initial letters of several and tequilas

explanation.surface: Wanting the first of several tequilas in a pub, as a matter of theory.
explanation.walkthrough: Also the title of David Bowie's final album, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A black star is a hypothetical astronomical object predicted by theoretical physics, an alternative to the black hole.

clue.text: Is outside agitating and rabble- rousing

indicators.note: agitating means stirring up, so the letters of Is outside are shaken into new order

explanation.surface: Someone stands outside agitating, stirring up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech or conduct inciting people to rebel against authority is seditious, a near synonym of inflammatory.

clue.text: Ever-changing tiny tree

definitions.note: ever, as in for ever, stands as a noun for endless time

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of tiny tree are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tiny tree that keeps changing its appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ever-changing' reads as one adjective, but the hyphen splits definition from anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: For ever means for all time, so ever stands for infinite time without end.

clue.text: State restricting a motion for the Sabbath

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the state word encloses the rest

parts.note: to state something is to say it
a motion is a bowel movement, of which a turd is the product

explanation.surface: A state restricts a parliamentary motion concerning the Sabbath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motion' suggests a parliamentary proposal, but here it is the lavatorial sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In Judaism the day of rest falls on the seventh day of the week, from Friday sunset.

clue.text: A French girl covering weekend as 13, supposedly

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: covering means the girl's name wraps round the end of week

parts.note: Lucy is a girl's name
the end of the word week is the letter K

explanation.surface: A French girl covers the weekend shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weekend' reads as Saturday and Sunday, but splits into week + end, the last letter of week. Thirteen is traditionally an ill-omened number.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirteen is superstitiously held to bring bad luck, so the number is supposedly ill-fated.

clue.text: Mother shunned mayo: badly lacks some egg

indicators.note: shunned says the mother word is pushed out of mayo

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: badly says the letters of lacks are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mother refuses mayonnaise because it is short of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: The yolk sac is a membrane-enclosed part of an egg or embryo, so it is part of an egg.

clue.text: House in which you sleep in Paris

parts.note: tu is the French for you, the setting in Paris applying to both words
dors is the French for sleep, as in you sleep

explanation.surface: A house in which a guest sleeps while in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' signals French; 'in which' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the royal dynasty ruling England from 1485 to 1603; a royal family is a house.

clue.text: A card for Neil's sixtieth

definitions.meaning: a playing card from the red suit marked with lozenges
the sixtieth anniversary or jubilee is named after a precious gem

explanation.surface: Buying a card for Neil's sixtieth birthday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neil's' nods to the singer Neil Diamond and acts as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Any card of the lozenge suit counts; and a sixtieth wedding anniversary or jubilee takes the name of the gemstone.

clue.text: Only half of sketch left? Talent is wasted

indicators.note: half of takes the first three letters of sketch, the first two of left and the first three of talent

explanation.surface: An artist leaves only half a sketch, a talent squandered.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wasted by illness is emaciated, thin as a bag of bones.

clue.text: Official could be desirable? No sir!

indicators.note: could be signals that letters of desirable are rearranged
No says the letters of sir are not part of the answer and are taken from the pool

explanation.surface: Is an official desirable? No sir, comes the indignant reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S, I, R from DESIRABLE and rearrange the remaining DEABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A beadle is a minor parish or church officer, keeping order in services.

clue.text: Weapon that's commemorated here

definitions.meaning: a large sheath knife named after the frontiersman Jim
the puzzle is a tribute to the musician David, whose songs and albums fill the grid

explanation.definitionFit: The knife takes its name from Jim of the Alamo, and the late rock star is honoured by the theme.

clue.text: Out of practice on changing sides, becomes passionate

indicators.note: changing sides swaps right for left in the out-of-practice word

parts.note: rusty means out of practice

explanation.surface: An athlete out of practice switches sides and plays with new passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusty means vigorous and full of desire, just as passionate does.

clue.text: To begin with, on clean cuts, put round plaster

indicators.note: put round turns the sequence so it reads from end to start
to begin with takes the first letters of on and clean

explanation.surface: First aid advice: put a plaster on clean cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put round' reverses OC + CUTS. 'Plaster' suggests a sticking plaster; it is building render.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster or render used to coat walls and mould decorations.

clue.text: Like to come back to hospital having inferior outside support

indicators.note: come back means the like word is read backwards

parts.note: as can mean like

indicators.note: outside says the inferior word goes around the hospital letter

parts.note: worse means inferior
H is the abbreviation for hospital on maps and signs

explanation.surface: A patient returns to a hospital with poor support outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawhorse is a frame that supports wood while it is being sawn.

clue.text: Minority group holds back party

indicators.note: back means the hidden letters are read from right to left
holds signals the letters are held inside the words Minority group

explanation.surface: A minority group holds back from a party.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a wild party marked by excessive indulgence.

clue.text: Were pants not wet, we'd have left with nothing

parts.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so things that were pants sucked
dry means not wet

explanation.surface: A grumble that, had our trousers not been wet, we would have had nothing left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers but is the British slang adjective for bad.
explanation.definitionFit: To be drained of all resources, leaving nothing behind, is idiomatically to be drained completely.
